description: Verify that DHCPDISCOVER 'chaddr' field carries the DUT iface MAC — the hardware address identifying the client (RFC 2131 §4.4.1 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
The server uses chaddr to look up / pin the client's MAC↔IP binding. RFC 2131 §4.4.1 requires chaddr to be the DUT's actual interface MAC; a zero or fake value would either fail lookup or pollute neighbour bookkeeping.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT → wire: DHCPDISCOVER
   • chaddr == DUT iface MAC   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DISCOVER chaddr matches the DUT's outgoing iface MAC.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_chaddr_mismatch — DISCOVER chaddr is not the DUT iface MAC
• Fail_no_discover — DUT did not emit DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window

verdicts.Pass: DISCOVER chaddr = DUT iface MAC — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
